items.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers | MIT News | Massachusetts Institute of Technology
items.summary:
### AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands

The new approach, known as FLEX, could lead to more intuitive, interactive household and assistive robots.

Read full story →

Man wearing a T-shirt and safety goggles standing above a concrete beam in the lab, operating a bench-mounted laser tool scanning the concrete.

### Fabric molds could bring material-saving concrete beams within reach [...] ### MIT scientists debut a generative AI model that could create molecules addressing hard-to-treat diseases

Christopher Voigt and Eszter Majer (pictured) collaborated with chloroplast and mitochondria experts from the Max Planck Institute of Molecular Plant Physiology in Germany and the Polytechnic University of Madrid, Spain, during their seed grant period, collaborations that were made possible by J-WAFS seed grants.

### Making real a biotechnology dream: nitrogen-fixing cereal crops [...] The first greenhouse tests of initial RNAi candidates are expected to be complete by the end of the first year of the program.

As part of this project, the research team will also develop living microbial systems that degrade agrochemicals before they reach food, soil, or waterways. Engineered bacteria, fungi, and srRNA will convert chemicals and formulation ingredients into biomass, providing a scalable strategy to reduce environmental and human exposure.

items.title: Catching Our Eye News Roundup, Nov. 10, 2026 • Ohio Capital Journal
items.summary:
About 30 days before Republicans suffered their biggest midterm election in decades this week, party leaders in the Statehouse made a big promise to drivers to temporarily cut Ohio’s gas tax, starting just as early voting began.

As planned, gas prices listed on retailers’ signs would fall the whole 38.5 cents per gallon (47 cents per gallon of diesel) for the 90-day “gas tax holiday.” [...] But the savings haven’t made it to customers, at least according to about 200 Ohioans who filed complaints with the Ohio Attorney General’s Office.

• State budget. The Statehouse News Bureau’s Sarah Donaldson reports, “Blue governor, red legislature: How will Ohio budget unfold next year?”

When she takes the reins in January, Democratic Governor-elect Amy Acton has to begin work on her 2028-2029 executive budget proposal almost immediately. [...] After the inauguration, Acton has just two months to get her ideas on how Ohio will or won’t fund various agencies and services to members of the Ohio General Assembly. The executive budget proposal is due to lawmakers by March 15.

She, through Democrats in both legislative chambers, will then need to find common ground with Republicans. They still hold majorities in the Ohio House and the Ohio Senate, even after losing ground Tuesday night.

items.title: Trump defends Jensen Huang at press briefing with UFC’s Dana White
items.summary:
In his first post-midterm news briefing, President Donald Trump on Monday talked about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy, the effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the massive Republican losses at the ballot box last week. [...] People familiar with the matter told NBC News on Sunday that U.S. intelligence agencies had determined that Alice Huang, the woman with whom Jensen Huang allegedly had the affair, was a Chinese spy. The two are not related.

Trump said that he had spoken to Huang on Monday “just to see if he’s feeling alright.”

“He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Trump said, adding that Huang is a “very honorable man.”
